questions.question: Tso Kar wetland has been included in Ramsar Site in December 2020. In which of the following states or union territories is it located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Ladakh__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__ 

__
 
• India has added Tso Kar Wetland Complex in Ladakh as its **42nd Ramsar site**, which is the second one in the Union Territory (UT) of **Ladakh**.
 
• The Tso Kar Basin is a high-altitude wetland complex, consisting of two principal waterbodies, Startsapuk Tso, a freshwater lake of about 438 hectares to the south, and Tso Kar itself, a hypersaline lake of 1800 hectares to the north, situated in the Changthang region of Ladakh, India.
 
 
• It is called Tso Kar, meaning **white lake**, because of the white salt efflorescence found on the margins due to the evaporation of highly saline water.
 
 
 
• The Tso Kar Basin is an A1 Category Important Bird Area (IBA) as per BirdLife International and a key staging site in the Central Asian Flyway.
 
• The site is also one of the most important **breeding areas of the Black-necked Crane (Grus nigricollis) in India.**
 
 
• This IBA is also the major breeding area for Great Crested Grebe (Podicepscristatus), Bar-headed Geese (Anserindicus), Ruddy Shelduck (Tadornaferruginea), Brown-headed Gull (Larusbrunnicephalus), Lesser Sand-Plover (Charadriusmongolus), and many other species.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__ 

 
• The **aim of the Ramsar list** is “to develop and maintain an international network of wetlands which are important for the conservation of global biological diversity and for sustaining human life through the maintenance of their ecosystem components, processes, and benefits”.
 
• Wetlands provide a wide range of important resources and ecosystem services such as food, water, fibre, groundwater recharge, water purification, flood moderation, erosion control and climate regulation.
 
 
• They are, in fact a major source of water and our main supply of freshwater comes from an array of wetlands that help soak rainfall and recharge groundwater.
 
• The Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change would be working closely with the UT Wetland Authority to ensure wise use of this site.

questions.question: ______ is a naturally occurring phenomenon that is responsible for the heating of the Earth’s surface and atmosphere.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Greenhouse effect.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The greenhouse effect **is a process that occurs when **gases in Earth's atmosphere trap the Sun's heat.**
 
• This process **makes Earth much warmer **than it would be without an atmosphere.
 
• A **greenhouse **is a **building with glass walls and a glass roof **and used to grow plants.
 
• It leads to an **increase in the Earth's temperature **because the glass walls of the greenhouse trap the Sun's heat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Radiation **is the energy that comes from a source and travels through space at the speed of light like heat, light, ultraviolet rays, etc.
 
• The **increase **in the **Earth's average temperature **over the past few decades is called **Global warming.**
 
• **Global warming **occurs when **carbon dioxide (CO2) **and other **air pollutants **and **greenhouse gases **are **collected in the atmosphere **and absorb sunlight and solar **radiation **that have **bounced off the earth’s surface.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ionosphere is NOT correct?

options.text: Radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
It is ionized by solar and cosmic radiation.
It is located immediately above the stratopause.

questions.solution:
The **Ionosphere** is the ionized part of Earth's upper atmosphere, which extends from about **__60 km to 1,000 km__** altitude.

 
• The ionosphere is a very active part of the atmosphere, and it grows and shrinks depending on the energy it absorbs from the Sun.
 
• It contains charged particles and is ionized by solar radiation.
 
• The ionosphere is a region that includes the thermosphere and parts of the **mesosphere** and **exosphere**.

questions.question: DDT adversely affects our environment because:

options.text: it can kill beneficial insects like honey bees
it can allow growth of harmful insects
it can promote growth of harmful insects

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**it can kill beneficial insects like honey bees.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• DDT is **very insoluble in water and very persistent in the environment, making it a highly polluting hazard**.
 
• Its half-life has been reported to be between **2 and 15 years.**
 
• DDT (dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethane) was developed as the first of the **modern synthetic insecticides** in the 1940s.
 
• It was initially used with great effect to **combat malaria, typhus, and other insect-borne human diseases among both military and civilian populations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Insecticides are **chemicals used to control insects by killing them or preventing them from engaging in undesirable or destructive behaviours**.
 
• Organic pesticides are usually considered as those **pesticides that come from natural sources**. 
 
• Synthetic** contact insecticides** are now the **primary agents of insect control**.​ 
 
• Inorganic insecticides are **of mineral origin, mainly compounds of antimony, arsenic, barium, boron, copper, fluorine, mercury, selenium, sulfur, thallium, and zinc, and elemental phosphorus and sulfur**.

questions.question: Eutrophication is a condition where excessive growth of algal bloom occurs on the surface of a water body because of abundant nutrients. Which of the following are the key nutrients for eutrophication?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phosphorus and Nitrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is the process where an excessive amount of nutrients leads to rapid growth of algae, commonly referred to as algal blooms, in water bodies.
 
• **Phosphorus (P)** and **Nitrogen (N)** are the two primary nutrients responsible for eutrophication, as they act as fertilizers for algal growth.
 
• Phosphorus is often introduced into water bodies through agricultural runoff containing fertilizers, detergents, and untreated sewage.
 
• Nitrogen primarily enters water systems from sources like fertilizers, livestock waste, and industrial discharges.
 
• The excessive algal growth reduces oxygen levels in the water, leading to the death of aquatic organisms and severely impacting biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Algal Bloom:** A rapid increase or accumulation of algae in water systems, often visible as green, red, or brown discoloration on the water surface.
 
• **Hypoxia:** A condition where the oxygen levels in the water drop drastically due to the decomposition of algae, leading to "dead zones" where aquatic life cannot survive.
 
• **Sources of Nutrients:** Nutrient pollution is primarily caused by agricultural runoff, urban wastewater, industrial discharges, and improper disposal of fertilizers and detergents.
 
• **Impact on Ecosystems:** Eutrophication leads to biodiversity loss, disruption of food chains, and contamination of drinking water sources due to toxins produced by certain algal species.
 
• **Preventive Measures:** Managing agricultural practices, reducing fertilizer use, treating wastewater, and creating buffer zones near water bodies can help control eutrophication.

questions.question: The process by which a water body gradually becomes enriched with nutrients and minerals, mainly phosphorus and nitrogen, leading to enormous growth of algae on the surface of the water, thus decreasing the amount of dissolved oxygen in the water is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eutrophication**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is the process by which a water body becomes enriched with nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, leading to excessive growth of algae.
 
• This phenomenon often results from **runoff of fertilizers, sewage, and industrial waste** into water bodies.
 
• The excessive algae growth, also called **algal bloom**, blocks sunlight penetration into the water.
 
• As algae die and decompose, the process consumes large amounts of **dissolved oxygen**, creating oxygen-depleted zones.
 
• Low oxygen levels (hypoxia) can lead to the death of aquatic organisms, disrupting the **ecosystem balance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biomagnification**: The process by which the concentration of toxins increases as they move up the food chain, affecting top predators most severely.
 
• **Hypoxia**: A condition where oxygen levels in water are too low to sustain aquatic life, often a result of eutrophication.
 
• **Bioaccumulation**: The accumulation of harmful substances, such as pesticides or heavy metals, in an organism over time.
 
• **Point and Non-Point Sources**: Nutrient pollution causing eutrophication can originate from point sources (e.g., factories) or non-point sources (e.g., agricultural runoff).
 
• **Dead Zones**: Areas in water bodies where oxygen levels are too low to support life, often caused by eutrophication. The Gulf of Mexico is a well-known example.

questions.question: What are the dissolved and suspended impurities in sewage called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**The dissolved and suspended impurities in sewage are generally referred to as **contaminants or pollutants**.*** Hence, Option 4 is correct.***

These can be further categorized into various types, including:

 
• **Organic matter:** Such as human waste, food scraps, and soaps.
 
• **Nutrients**: Including nitrogen and phosphorus compounds, which can promote excessive growth of algae in water bodies (eutrophication).
 
• **Pathogens**: Bacteria, viruses, and parasites that can cause diseases.
 
• **Chemicals:** These can include pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and industrial chemicals.
 
• **Microplastics**: Small plastic particles that persist in the environment.
 
• **Heavy metals**: Such as lead, mercury, and cadmium, which are toxic to aquatic life and humans.

The solid particles that are suspended in wastewater are often referred to as "suspended solids," while the dissolved ones can be nutrients, certain organic compounds, or other soluble materials. Proper treatment of sewage is necessary to remove or reduce these impurities before the water is released back into the environment or reused.

questions.question: Tiger belongs to which category under IUCN?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct:

__
 
• The **IUCN Red List** of threatened species classifies Tigers as **Endangered**__.
 
• Tiger populations have plummeted from around 100,000 individuals in 1910 to 3,200 individuals in 2010, occupying 7% of their original range.
 
• Initiated in 2014, the Integrated **Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme (ITHCP)** or **‘Tiger Programme‘** is a grant-making initiative which contributes to the Global Tiger Recovery Programme (GTRP), a global effort to double tiger numbers in the wild by **2022**.
 
• The programme consists of a portfolio of 12 large-scale projects in key Tiger Conservation Landscapes across Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Indonesia, Nepal and Myanmar.
 
• The initiative is funded by **The German Cooperation via KfW Development Bank**, over two phases. The first phase is being implemented from 2014 to 2020 and the second one from 2019 to 2023.
 
• **India** became a State Member of IUCN in **1969**, through the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).

questions.question: ______ refers to a sanitation system in which toilets collect human excreta in sealable, removable cartridges that are transported to treatment facilities.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Container-Based sanitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Container-based sanitation (CBS) **is a sanitation method in which toilets collect human waste and transport it to treatment facilities in **sealable, removable containers **(also known as cartridges).
 
• This method of sanitation entails the use of a commercial service that offers specific types of portable toilets and distributes empty containers when full ones are picked up. The service carries excreta and carefully disposes of or reuses it.
 
• The users are normally responsible for the cost of excreta collection. CBS can be utilised to offer low-income urban areas safe collection, transportation, and treatment of faeces at a lesser cost than establishing and maintaining sewers with the right development, support, and collaborations.
 
• **Sanitation systems **based on containers are a low-cost option. They can be employed in quickly increasing cities, refugee camps, and disaster relief circumstances.
 
• They are in line with Sustainable Development Goal 6 of the United Nations, which is to "provide sanitation for all by 2030."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ecological sanitation** is a method of sanitation that tries to safely reuse human waste in agriculture.
 
• It is a concept, not a technology or a device, that is defined by a goal to "complete the loop" between sanitation and agriculture in a safe manner, primarily for nutrients and organic matter.
 
• The disposal of human waste without the use of water as a carrier is known as **dry sanitation.**
 
• **CLTS (Community Led Total Sanitation)** is an innovative approach to mobilizing communities to prevent open defecation (OD). Communities are given the tools they need to assess and analyze open defecation (OD) and take steps to achieve ODF (open defecation free).

questions.question: What does 'C' stand for in ITCZ?
questions.solution:
In **ITCZ, "C" **is stand for __**Convergence**__.

 
• **The Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)** is the zone that covers the Earth, near the equator.
 
• Where trade winds from the Northern and Southern Hemispheres come together.
 
• The sun and warm water of the equator heat up the air in the** ITCZ, increase its temperature, and keep it buoyant. **
 
• With the aid of the convergence of the industrial winds, the buoyant air is rising.
 
• When the **air increases,** it spreads and cools, releasing concentrated heat in an almost endless cycle of thunderstorms.

questions.question: The condition, when the environment becomes enriched with nutrients, increasing the amount of plant and algae growth in estuaries and coastal waters, is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**eutrophication**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is the process by which a body of water becomes overly enriched with nutrients.
 
• This enrichment leads to an increase in the growth of plants and algae in the water.
 
• **Sources of nutrients** causing eutrophication include runoff from agriculture, wastewater discharge, and industrial effluents.
 
• **Algal blooms** can deplete the oxygen in the water, leading to dead zones where aquatic life cannot survive.
 
• Eutrophication can also result in the deterioration of water quality, affecting both **ecosystems and human health**.
 
• Management practices include reducing nutrient loads, improving wastewater treatment, and implementing sustainable agricultural practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mineralisation**__

 __
 
• **Mineralisation** refers to the process by which organic matter is decomposed to release inorganic nutrients.
 
• This process is crucial for the cycling of nutrients in ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Ozone depletion**__
 __
 
• **Ozone depletion** refers to the thinning of the Earth's ozone layer caused by chemicals like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).
 
• This depletion allows more harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation to reach the Earth's surface, affecting both human health and the environment.
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse effect**__
 
 
• The **greenhouse effect** is the process by which certain gases in the Earth's atmosphere trap heat, leading to an increase in global temperatures.
 
• Key greenhouse gases include carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O).
 
• This effect is crucial for maintaining the Earth's temperature but is currently exacerbated by human activities, leading to global warming.

questions.question: A pyramid of biomass is a diagram that shows the population at each level of the food chain. Accordingly, ________ occupy the base with the highest biomass.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**producers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **pyramid** of biomass is a graphical representation that shows the population at each level of the food chain. 
 
• **Producers** occupy the base with the highest biomass.
 
• The relationship between numbers, biomass, energy, or bio productivity of an ecosystem can be represented by a pyramid known as the **ecological pyramid.**
 
• **The trophic level **is the place that a living organism occupies in a food chain.
 
• In a biomass pyramid, **producers** are at the base, followed by **herbivores** and then **carnivores** at the top.
 
• The **pyramid** of biomass shows the flow of energy from producers to consumers.
 
• **10 percent** of the energy gets transferred to the next trophic level and the rest is either utilized for metabolic processes or excreted out.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Carnivores that eat herbivores are called** secondary consumers**.
 
• A separate trophic level, the **decomposers** or transformers, consists of organisms such as bacteria and fungi that break down dead organisms and waste materials into nutrients usable by the producers.
 
• **Primary consumers** make up the second trophic level. They are also called herbivores.

questions.question: Biotic potential can be defined as:

options.text: the minimum number of individuals of a species that can survive but cannot reproduce
the minimum number of individuals a species can produce
the maximum number of individuals a species can produce
the maximum number of individuals of a species that cannot survive after birth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the maximum number of individuals a species can produce**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Biotic potential** refers to the **maximum reproductive capacity** of an organism under optimum environmental conditions.
 
• This concept is significant in population ecology as it helps to understand the growth potential of a species.
 
• The **biotic potential** is influenced by factors such as the organism's rate of reproduction and the duration of its reproductive life.
 
• It is an idealized concept assuming no limiting factors like food scarcity, predation, or disease, which in reality always exist to some extent.
 
• The actual population size is often lower than the biotic potential due to these environmental resistance factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Understanding biotic potential is crucial for **conservation efforts** and managing species that are endangered or overpopulated.
 
• **Environmental resistance** includes all factors that limit the biotic potential of an organism, such as food availability, predation, disease, and habitat destruction.
 
• In practical terms, the biotic potential is rarely achieved in natural environments due to these limiting factors.
 
• Ecologists use the concept to model population growth and to predict how populations will respond to changes in environmental conditions.
 
• The study of biotic potential is part of **population ecology**, which examines the dynamics of species populations and how they interact with the environment.

questions.question: Who is the father of the modern ecology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The father of the modern ecology** is considered to be **Eugene Odum,** an American ecologist who is widely regarded as one of the pioneering figures in the development of modern ecology.
 
• **Odum **is known for his groundbreaking work on ecosystem ecology, which focuses on the relationships between living organisms and their physical environment.
 
• He also developed the concept of** "ecosystem," **which is a functional unit of living organisms and their physical environment.
 
• Odum's work has had a significant impact on the field of ecology, and he is credited with helping to establish ecology as a distinct scientific discipline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Robert Brown was a Scottish botanist and biologist who made significant contributions to various fields of science**.

• **Charles Darwin was an English naturalist and biologist who is best known for his contributions to the theory of evolution. **
 
 
• **He is famous for his book "On the Origin of Species," published in 1859, in which he proposed that all species of life **have evolved over time from a common ancestor through a process of natural selection.
 
• This theory revolutionized the field of biology and had a profound impact on scientific thinking and society as a whole.

questions.question: Eutrophication can be defined as:

options.text: the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an grassland ecosystem
the gradual decrease in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake
the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in desert areas
the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake.
 
• This process leads to an increase in the growth of algae and aquatic plants, which can deplete the oxygen levels in the water and harm aquatic life.
 
• Eutrophication is typically caused by runoff from agriculture, wastewater, and other nutrient sources entering the water body.
 
• It can result in harmful algal blooms, fish kills, and loss of biodiversity in aquatic ecosystems.
 
• Management practices such as reducing nutrient runoff and improving wastewater treatment can help mitigate eutrophication.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eutrophication** can also occur naturally over long periods, but human activities have accelerated the process significantly.
 
• In severe cases, eutrophication can create "dead zones" where oxygen levels are too low to support most marine life.
 
• Preventative measures include promoting sustainable agricultural practices, using phosphate-free detergents, and protecting wetlands that can filter nutrients.
 
• Public awareness and education on the impacts of nutrient pollution are crucial in addressing eutrophication.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs represents a parasitic relationship?

• A parasitic relationship is a relationship between two different organisms in which one organism gains at the expense of others without killing it.

• The relationship between **sharks and remora fish** is a **symbiotic relationship**.

questions.question: The green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem capture about _______ of the energy of sunlight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1%.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The **green plants** in a terrestrial ecosystem **capture about 1% of the energy** of sunlight that falls on their leaves and converts it into food energy.
 
• When **green plants** are **eaten by primary consumers**, a great deal of energy is lost as heat to the environment, some amount goes into digestion and in doing work and the rest goes towards growth and reproduction. An **average of 10% **of the food eaten is turned into its own body and made **available** for the **next level **of consumers.
 
• Therefore, **10% **can be taken as the **average value** for the amount of organic matter that is present at each step and reaches the next level of consumers.
 
• Since so **little energy is available for the next level of consumers**, food chains generally consist of only three or four steps. The loss of energy at each step is so great that very little usable energy remains after four trophic levels.
 
• There are generally a greater number of individuals at the lower trophic levels of an ecosystem, the greatest number is of the producers.

__

• In other words, the **environmental Kuznets curve suggests that economic development initially leads to a deterioration in the environment,** but after a **certain level of economic growth, a society begins to improve its relationship with the environment, and levels of environmental degradation reduce.**
 
• The EKC suggests that the **solution to pollution is economic growth**.

• The link **between levels of income and environmental degradation is quite weak.**

questions.question:
Consider following statements.

1) A system consisting of biotic and abiotic components is known as ecosystem. 

2) All the components of the ecosystem are inter-related.

3) Ecosystem always have clear boundaries.

Which statement is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2 statements are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Ecosystem: 

__
 
• All organisms such as plants, animals, microorganisms and human beings as well as the physical surroundings interact with each other and maintain a balance in nature.
 
• All the interacting organisms in an area together with the non-living constituents of the environment form an ecosystem.
 
• The term ecosystem was coined by Tansley.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/377faffe87f801fad37875fa8fe3fd5faa70648e1d3407f7e9052989a44ae655.png]

__Explanation:__

Components of an ecosystem:

Biotic Components: 

 
• It includes producers, consumers and decomposers.
 
• All living things have a direct or indirect influence on other organisms in an environment.
 
• Example: plants, animals, humans, microorganism etc.

Abiotic components: 

 
• All the in-organic components of the ecosystem, non-living physical and chemical composition of nature are abiotic components.
 
• Example: land, stones, water, humus (organic waste), air etc.

questions.question: In an ecosystem, vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**stratification**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of identification and enumeration of plant and animal species of an ecosystem gives its species composition.
 
• The vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called >stratification.
 
• For example, trees occupy the top vertical strata or layer of a forest, shrubs the second, and herbs and grasses occupy the bottom layers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Species composition**

 
 
• It differs from one ecosystem to another depending upon geography, topography, and climate.
 
• Each ecosystem has a biotic community composed of a particular grouping of species.
 
• Maximum species composition occurs in tropical rainforests and coral reefs.
 
• The minimum occurs in deserts and arctic regions.
 
 
 
• **Stratifications**
 
 
• Stratification is the occurrence of vertical zonation in the ecosystem & indicates the presence of favorable environmental conditions, for e.g., trees occupy top vertical strata or layer of a forest, shrubs, and herbs & grasses occupy the bottom layers. >Stratification helps in the accommodation of a large number & types of plants in the same area.
 
• It also provides a number of microhabitat & niches for various types of animals.
 
• It is absent or poor where environmental conditions are unfavorable, e.g. desert ecosystems have very few trees & shrubs.
 
 
 
• **Standing crop**
 
 
• A standing crop is an amount of living biomass in an ecosystem. It indicates the productivity & luxuriance of growth.
 
• It is expressed in the form of the number or biomass of organisms per unit area.
 
• A terrestrial ecosystem with a high standing crop possesses a forest while the one with a low standing crop occurs in grassland followed by the arid ecosystem.

questions.question: Which ecologist’s research provided revolutionary new insights into how energy and nutrients move through the ecosystems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raymond L Lindeman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raymond Laurel Lindeman **(**1915 – June 29, 1942**) was an **ecologist **whose **graduate research **is **credited with being a seminal study in **the **field of ecosystem ecology**, **specifically **on the **topic of trophic dynamics**.
 
• **Lindeman completed **his **Ph.D**. at the **University of Minnesota **with his **thesis work **being concerned with the history and ecological dynamics of Cedar Bog Lake.
 
• **Some insights **of his research:
 
 
• **Energy is passed from one trophic level **to the **next trophic level**.
 
• Hence, **energy flows **in one **direction **through **successive trophic levels **in **a food chain**.
 
• **Nutrients **are **produced from the matter**. The **matter **may be **organic **or **inorganic**.
 
• The **organic **and **inorganic matter **is produced, exchanged, and moved within the **ecosystem **and this is **called cycling**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sir Arthur George Tansley **FLS, FRS (**15 August 1871 – 25 November 1955**) was an **English botanist **and a **pioneer **in the science of ecology.
 
• **Ernst Heinrich Philipp August Haeckel **was a **German zoologist**, **naturalist**, **eugenicist**, **philosopher**, **physician**, **professor**, **marine biologist, and artist**.
 
• **Charles Sutherland **Elton FRS (**29 March 1900 – 1 May 1991**) was an **English zoologist **and **animal ecologist**.

questions.question: Which level of the food chain includes Typha bulrushes, Sagittaria, Hydrilla, Rupia, Chara, occurring in concentric layers from the periphery to the deep regions?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rooted plants **occur in **concentric layers** from the **periphery to the deeper zones.**
 
• Some examples of rooted plants are **Typha bulrushes, Sagittaria, Hydrilla, Rupia, and Chara.**
 
• They are **producers **in the food chain.
 
• **Producers:**
 
 
• **Autotrophs** are another name for producers.
 
• They produce their **own food.**
 
• Every** food chain's initial level **is comprised of them.
 
• **Plants or single-celled organisms **are the majority of autotrophs.
 
• The majority of autotrophs produce their** "food"** from **sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water **through a process known as** photosynthesis.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Primary consumers:**

 
 
• The **second trophic level** consists of primary consumers.
 
• **Herbivores** is another name for them.
 
• They consume **primary producers**, such as plants or algae. 
 
 
 
• **Secondary consumers:**
 
 
• The majority of secondary consumers are** carnivores.**
 
• They eat the** primary consumers,** which are herbivores.
 
• These organisms are **heterotrophs**, more particularly, **omnivores and carnivores.**
 
 
 
• **Decomposers:**
 
 
• Decomposers are creatures that perform **decomposition** or the **breakdown of dead or decaying organisms.**

questions.question: In the context of various environment protection treaties/protocols and the places associated with them, which of the following is NOT correctly paired?

• **Stockholm Convention** deals with **Persistent Organic Pollutants**. It is a global treaty that focuses on health protection as well as environmental protection. Adopted on** 22nd May 2001 **and entered into force on **17th May 2004**.
 
• The **Basel Convention** deals with the **control of transboundary movements of hazardous wastes** and their disposal. This convention was adopted on 22 March 1989.
 
• **Nagoya Protocol** is an international agreement focussing on **shared benefits** that arise from the **utilization of genetic resources in a fair and equitable manner**. Came into effect in October 2014.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best definition of ecological efficiency?

options.text: The amount of energy utilised at different trophic levels in a food chain
The amount of energy stored at different trophic levels in a food chain
The ratio between the mass and the energy flow at different trophic levels in a food chain
The ratio between energy flows at different points in a food chain

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The ratio between energy flows at different points in a food chain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ecological efficiency refers to the efficiency with which energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next in a food chain.
 
• Typically, only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is passed on to the next level; this is known as the 10% law.
 
• This concept helps in understanding the energy dynamics and the structure of ecosystems.
 
• Higher trophic levels receive less energy, which explains why there are typically fewer organisms at higher levels in a food chain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trophic Levels**

 
 
• In ecology, a trophic level is the position that an organism occupies in a food chain.
 
• Primary producers (plants) are at the first trophic level, primary consumers (herbivores) at the second, secondary consumers (carnivores that eat herbivores) at the third, and so on.
 
 
 
• **Energy Flow**
 
 
• Energy flow in an ecosystem is one-way: from the sun to producers, then to consumers, and finally to decomposers.
 
• Energy is lost at each trophic level, primarily as heat resulting from metabolism.
 
 
 
• **10% Law**
 
 
• The 10% law states that only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next trophic level.
 
• This rule was first introduced by Raymond Lindeman in 1942.
 
 
 
• **Food Chain**
 
 
• A food chain is a linear sequence of organisms through which nutrients and energy pass as one organism eats another.
 
• In a food chain, each organism occupies a different trophic level.

questions.question: Which district has been awarded the Plastic Waste Management Award -2020 for being the best district of India in the plastic waste management category during Swachhta Hi Seva 2019?
questions.solution:
__**Dibrugarh**__ has been awarded the **Plastic Waste Management Award -2020** for being the best district of India in the plastic waste management category during **Swachhta Hi Seva 2019.**

 
• **Swachhta Hi Seva on Swachhta is a huge nationwide program of awareness and mobilization.**
 
• The 2019 Swachhta hi Seva was held from **11 September till 2 October 2019.**
 
• PM Modi had set the goal of making India ODF** under the Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) by October 2, the 150th anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi's birth.**
 
• On October 2 the initiative also included a nationwide shramdaan for **collecting and segregating plastic waste.**
